data.title: Explained - The key trigger behind Paytm, Pine Labs, MobiKwik shares fell up to 8% on Thursday
data.description:
Shares of One97 Communications Ltd., parent company of payments aggregator Paytm, along with its peers, Pine Labs Ltd., and One MobiKwik Ltd., fell up to 8% on Thursday, November 19, after CNBC-TV18 reported that the rollout date for the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) still remains unclear.

While shares of Paytm were down over 7%, those of Pine Labs fell up to 4.5%, and those of One MobiKwik Solutions are down over 8% on Thursday.

Sources said that business-to-business payments through UPI could see a separate pricing structure, with a flat ₹5 charge proposed for merchant-to-merchant transactions.

The sources went on to add that the NPCI UPI and Services steering committee had cleared the proposal around a month ago, but the decision has not been formally notified yet.

In a note on November 18, Pranav Gundlapalle of Bernstein wrote that Paytm is well positioned for non-linear earnings growth, driven by operating leverage, and continued growth in financial services, particularly merchant lending, with MDR on UPI representing a key near-term catalyst.

We assess the key risks to our investment thesis beyond a weaker-than-expected operating trajectory. None appears particularly threatening in the near to medium term, but as expectations rise, so does the relevance of understanding the downside risks.PRANAV GUNDLAPALLE, BERNSTEIN ON PAYTM

Two potential risks standout for Paytm, according to the Bernstein note, which include caps on IRRs in merchant lending and changes to the current digital lending model.

"The most immediate risk is the non-implementation or indefinite postponement of MDR on UPI which remains a key driver of near-term earnings growth," Bernstein wrote in its note.

Yet, Bernstein continues to find the risk-reward attractive for Paytm, and has therefore maintained its "buy" recommendation on the stock with a price target of ₹2,200.

Shares of Paytm are trading 6.2% lower on Thursday at ₹1,773, while those of Pine Labs are trading 3.5% lower at ₹163.5. Shares of One MobiKwik Solutions are also trading 6.5% lower on Thursday at ₹211.8. Both Paytm and Pine Labs are the top losers on the Nifty 500 index.

(MDR Newsbreak By Ritu Singh)

data.title: Trump Announces $17 Billion in Southeast Asia Deals
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong and Amanda Lee

The U.S. has secured a series of investment and trade deals across Southeast Asia as it seeks to expand its economic presence in the region.

President Trump announced more than $17 billion in commercial deals and strategic investments benefiting U.S. companies following a two-day state visit to the Philippines and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit, the White House said Wednesday.

Trump and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. announced deals aimed at narrowing the U.S. trade deficit with the Philippines by increasing Philippine imports of American energy and agricultural products, the White House said.

Boeing and GE Aerospace finalized a $12 billion deal to supply Philippine Airlines with up to 20 Boeing 787 aircraft. Washington also plans to pursue a military financing package worth more than $2 billion to provide the Philippines with U.S. defense equipment.

The U.S. and Thailand also made substantial progress toward a trade agreement that would eliminate tariffs on 99% of goods once signed and remove barriers to U.S. exports of vehicles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals and agricultural products.

Thailand also plans to spend up to $123 million on U.S.-made High Mobility Artillery Rocket Systems, the White House said.

In Indonesia, U.S.-based Latitude Energy and sovereign wealth fund Danantara announced talks on a $2 billion project to use American technology to improve the country's use of its coal resources.

U.S.-based Navajo Transitional Energy also signed a three-year, $100 million agreement to supply coal from its mine in southern Montana to Malaysia's TNB Fuel Services, a fuel procurement unit of utility Tenaga Nasional.

The announcements come as Southeast Asian economies grapple with higher U.S. tariffs while negotiating trade agreements with Washington.

Trade in goods and services between the U.S. and Asean totaled an estimated $686 billion in 2025, up 20.3% from 2024, according to the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative.

data.title: Indian payments stocks fall as UPI fee rollout faces delay
data.description:
Shares of Indian digital payments firms fell on Thursday over a delay in introducing transaction fees on the country's popular instant payments network, called the Unified Payments Interface.

One 97 Communications , Paytm's parent, was down 6.3% to 1,769.20 rupees, while shares of Pine Labs dropped 3.7% to 163 rupees and One Mobikwik Systems slid 7.3% to 210 rupees.

In September, the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) announced a 0.4% fee on merchant payments above 2,000 rupees ($20.84) from October 15, ending six years of free transactions.

The roll out was postponed until after Diwali earlier this month, following retailer opposition, with no new implementation date announced.

Three sources familiar with the discussions said a final decision on the date of implementation - likely to be made in consultation with the central bank and the government - is yet to be taken.

A delay in implementation cannot be ruled out, the sources said.

The NPCI and the federal finance ministry did not immediately respond to Reuters emails seeking comments.

data.title: North Korea shows off AI chatbot at IT exhibition, think tank 38 North says
data.description:
North Korea appears to have developed its first artificial intelligence chatbot, according to analysis by 38 North, a think tank that monitors North Korea, of footage broadcast on state television.

Here are the details:

  • The system, called "AI Service System 1.0, Fountain of Wisdom", was displayed at the National Exhibition of IT Successes in Pyongyang, held from October 19 to 30, according to 38 North. It featured in a report on Ryongnamsan TV on November 17.

  • It was built by Kim Il Sung University's Artificial Intelligence Technology Research Institute and Phurunhanul Trading Co, a Pyongyang software developer, 38 North said.

  • The chatbot can answer questions on science and technology in Korean or English and provide translations.

  • An on-screen warning instructs users not to ask socio-political questions, according to 38 North. The footage also appears to show a classifier screening queries before they reach the AI engine.

  • The hardware running the system was not disclosed. The 38 North report said the model behind the interface was more likely an open-weight system from a US or Chinese laboratory, such as Google's Gemma or Alibaba's Qwen, than one developed entirely in North Korea.

  • The report said the lack of large-scale data centres in North Korea could hamper deployment of the most advanced models.

data.title: Lenovo Maintains Revenue Momentum on AI-Fueled Hardware Demand
data.description:
(04:03 GMT) *Lenovo Group 2Q Rev $30.24B Vs. $20.45B >0992.HK
(04:03 GMT) *Lenovo Group 2Q Loss $640M Vs. Net $340M >0992.HK
(04:04 GMT) *Lenovo Group 2Q Adjusted Net $1.36B Vs. Net $512M >0992.HK
(04:08 GMT) *Lenovo Group 2Q Intelligent Devices Group Rev $17.37B Vs. $15.11B >0992.HK
(04:08 GMT) *Lenovo Group 2Q Infrastructure Services Group Rev $11.34B Vs. $4.09B >0992.HK
(04:09 GMT) *Lenovo: AI-Related Rev Made Up 36% of 2Q Rev >0992.HK
(04:28 GMT) Lenovo Maintains Revenue Momentum on AI-Fueled Hardware Demand

By Sherry Qin

Lenovo Group reported robust sales in the fiscal second quarter, on track to achieve its $100 billion annual revenue goal thanks to strong artificial-intelligence infrastructure demand.

Surging demand for AI servers and enterprise infrastructure has enabled the world's largest personal-computer maker to achieve better-than-expected results recently, offsetting a broader downturn in global PC shipments.

The company on Thursday said revenue for the three months ended September jumped 48% from a year earlier to $30.24 billion, beating market expectations.

Its adjusted net profit more than doubled to $1.36 billion, higher than analysts' estimate of $1.27 billion in a Visible Alpha poll. However, its bottom line was hit by a noncash fair-value loss arising from the revaluation of warrants, resulting in net loss of $640 million.

The company's infrastructure-solutions business, encompassing data-center hardware like AI servers, remained the biggest earnings driver. Segment revenue more than doubled from a year earlier, translating to operating profit of $1.09 billion.

Lenovo has been leveraging demand in the U.S., where the largest market opportunity for infrastructure currently resides. That could present challenges for its AI infrastructure business, especially after some cloud-service providers faced severe financial distress and Democrats swept the U.S. midterm elections.

Shares of Lenovo have swung wildly in recent quarters, mirroring these concerns. The stock has wiped out the 50% advance it made in the three months ended September, trimming its gains for the year to about 80%.

Despite a memory crunch and rising consumer-electronics prices, Lenovo has handled the headwinds relatively well. Its intelligent-devices group, which includes PCs, smartphones and tablets, posted 15% revenue growth.

That came as global PC shipments fell 20% in July to September, according to industry tracker IDC. Continued supply constraints and the inventory pull-in earlier in the year, as vendors and channels rushed to stock up ahead of memory-chip-driven price hikes, left the quarter with little demand to draw on.

Lenovo remained the world's largest PC maker by shipments during the quarter, with a 23.8% market share.

data.title: BOJ's Ueda Vows to Keep Careful Eye on Fed Moves — Update
data.description:
By Megumi Fujikawa

TOKYO--Bank of Japan Gov. Kazuo Ueda pledged to closely watch how Federal Reserve policy changes affect growth and inflation in Japan, while reaffirming his readiness to keep tightening monetary settings.

"With the Fed raising interest rates and many other central banks pivoting toward hikes, we need to carefully monitor how those rate moves and the accompanying changes in global financial conditions affect Japan's economy and prices," Ueda told a parliamentary committee on Thursday.

Ueda noted that currency fluctuations--which can be heavily swayed by Fed policy--are more likely to affect domestic prices than in the past as companies in Japan become more comfortable passing on costs to consumers.

"We will conduct monetary policy appropriately while keeping in mind that these shifts could in turn influence underlying inflation through changes in inflation expectations," he added.

While BOJ policymakers are cautious about cooling the economy with monetary tightening, further action looks necessary to keep inflation in check, especially as heightened expectations for Fed rate hikes pressure the yen.

Market participants see a growing chance that the BOJ could raise rates again as soon as December. The Fed is also widely expected to hike next month as U.S. inflation continues to concern officials.

The BOJ is keeping an eye on inflation too. Ueda again stressed the importance of anchoring underlying consumer inflation around 2% so it doesn't overshoot the central bank's target and hurt the economy.

He warned that one measure of underlying inflation--consumer prices excluding fresh food--is likely to accelerate clearly above 2% as firms pass on higher labor costs, oil remains expensive and yen weakness persists. Surging global demand related to the artificial-intelligence buildout adds another inflationary impulse.

In September, that gauge of underlying inflation accelerated to 2.1% year-on-year from August's 1.7%. Economists polled by data provider Quick expect October figures due Friday to show a further rise to 2.3%.

The BOJ said last month that underlying inflation had reached its 2% target for the first time since the goal was introduced in 2013. It held policy settings steady at its previous meeting in October after raising rates to 1.25% in September.

Despite the rate hikes delivered so far, the BOJ governor still sees Japan's financial conditions as accommodative, although he acknowledged that monetary tightening is affecting households and businesses through higher mortgage rates and funding costs.

"The bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation, in response to developments in economic activity and prices as well as financial conditions," he said.

data.title: India begins evacuations ahead of third cyclone within a month
data.description:
By Jatindra Dash

India's eastern state of Odisha evacuated more than 47,000 people by Thursday, before the region's third severe cyclonic storm in less than a month is set to hit land.

  • Cyclone Akvan is likely to cross the coastal states of Odisha and southern neighbouring Andhra Pradesh by noon on Friday, weather officials said, with heavy rain expected on Thursday

  • Odisha evacuated more than 47,000 people, the office of its chief minister said. Authorities also ordered the closure of all schools and kindergarten centres in some districts

  • "No evacuations in Andhra Pradesh yet," state disaster management official Prakhar Jain told Reuters. "The storm has reduced in intensity"

  • Andhra Pradesh evacuated thousands of coastal dwellers this month ahead of severe cyclonic storm Murasu, while Cyclone Arnab, in late October, killed at least six

  • "The pattern (of three cyclones within a month) in 2026 is mostly similar to that of 1987," top government weather expert Mrutyunjay Mohapatra told Reuters

  • After the 1987 monsoon, three cyclonic storms struck in the Bay of Bengal in quick succession

data.title: Ledger expands hardware hack investigation to Germany, UAE as new cases emerge
data.description:
Crypto hardware wallet maker Ledger has expanded its investigation into a physical supply-chain tampering campaign to Germany and the United Arab Emirates after identifying suspicious devices in Berlin and receiving loss reports in Dubai.

In a Wednesday update, the company said newly emerged cases were "the same incident" as ones involving tampered devices in Southeast Asia. It explained that it has confirmed the same kind of physical modification designed to capture the recovery phrase during setup.

"There is no flaw in Ledger's secure chip or operating system, and no confirmed case involving a device bought on ledger.com," Ledger stated in its update.

Ledger noted that it has progressed its investigation into reports of "a few tampered units" localized to Berlin, and urged anyone who purchased a device in the city from January to reach out to its support team.

In the UAE, the team has received reports of two tampered units in Dubai, and is investigating how they entered circulation. The company has also identified one case involving a newer model, the Ledger Nano Gen5, which was impacted in Southeast Asia.

Two X users, Rewinskyx and newbabylonorder, claimed to have lost a combined $604,000 in crypto from devices purchased at an authorized reseller in Dubai. The former reported losing about 1,300 SOL (SOL), while the latter said 507,000 USDT (USDT) was drained.

On Wednesday, Bitquery reported that roughly $1.68 million was stolen from 16 wallets in Dubai and Berlin, following the blockchain analytics firm's claim last month that the campaign drained about $102 million from 335 wallets in Southeast Asia.

Ledger has not officially confirmed the amount of losses from the supply chain tampering. The Block has reached out to Ledger for comment.

Origin

The expanded probe follows an investigation that began last month in Southeast Asia, where Ledger users reported unauthorized cryptocurrency drains. It was later identified that customers of authorized reseller CryptoBilis were targeted.

In a previous disclosure, Ledger stated that threat actors acquired genuine devices, installed additional custom-built hardware components to transmit recovery phrases externally, and reintroduced the units into reseller channels.

"As we continue our investigation, we expect it is possible that additional devices will be found, and we are working with partners and authorities to find affected devices as quickly as possible," Ledger said in the latest update. "This continues to be a small number of devices overall, and we do expect more to be discovered in our investigation and via social media."

data.title: In South Korea's make-or-break college exam, even a shirt button can raise suspicion
data.description:
Key points:
  • More than half a million students sitting the crucial university entrance exam
  • Exam faces intense scrutiny after scandal over AI-assisted cheating in other key test
  • Authorities scrambled to introduce a string of new measures to deter cheating
  • Aircraft will pause take-offs for 35 minutes during English audio section

By Maggie Grether and Soohyun Jung

As South Korean students sit the country's make-or-break university entrance exam on Thursday, they have more than tough questions to worry about. They also feel they must avoid looking like cheats.

More than half a million students across the country are taking the exam, an eight-hour marathon that tests subjects from mathematics to Korean and is crucial to securing a place at a top university in the hyper-competitive country.

The exam has faced intense scrutiny this year after the top scorer in this year's national tax accountant exam admitted on Sunday to using a microcamera and an AI tool to cheat, sparking a crisis of faith in the country's test-based education system.

The scandal left authorities scrambling to introduce new measures to deter cheating, ranging from banning candidates from bringing their own pens and erasers to placing stickers on any clothing buttons that could hide microcameras.

At one test venue in the centre of Seoul, some students said the AI-cheating scandal and the new rules had made them anxious and they had changed the way they prepared for the exam.

"Now, I wonder if it would have been better to postpone the exam altogether, and come up with a proper plan," said high-school student Kwak Yoo-Min, who originally planned to wear clothes with buttons, but instead opted for a T-shirt because he was afraid of being suspected of cheating.

Jang San, another high-school student, said he hoped all candidates would take the test fairly and honestly.

The government has said it plans to tighten rules so that anyone caught cheating is banned from taking the exam for 10 years, while also facing criminal penalties.

President Lee Jae Myung called in a post on X for rewards of at least 100 million won ($75,040) for people who reported cheating attempts.

"I had worked hard and thought I was doing just as well as everyone else," said 18-year-old Jang. "But all that effort could potentially go to waste because someone uses AI just once."

At 8:30 a.m. authorities sent an emergency alert to mobile devices across the country so that they would blare at maximum volume, in a bid to detect any devices smuggled into classrooms.

The education ministry later said that authorities confiscated 22 smartphones from students at exam centres and would investigate whether they were being used for cheating.

Across South Korea, authorities take extraordinary steps to ensure those taking the papers do so under optimal conditions.

Financial markets opened an hour later on Thursday, while aircraft will not be allowed to take off for 35 minutes during the English audio section of the test to minimise distracting noise.

Police also have vehicles on standby around the country to transport students running late to test centres.

($1 = 1,332.5900 won)

data.title: Pony AI's Shares Tumble as Regulatory Environment Reassessed
data.description:
By Jiahui Huang

Pony AI's shares tumbled Thursday as investors reassessed the outlook for the robotaxi industry, and after it reported a wider loss for the third quarter .

The autonomous driving company on Wednesday reported a net loss of $105.6 million, widening from $61.3 million in the same period a year earlier, even as revenue climbed 76% to $44.6 million.

The rise in revenue was a positive for the company and the widened loss was largely on losses on traded securities, rather than operational losses. But sentiment for the stock has been hurt by as investors reevaluate risks for the industry. There are concerns that growth may be slower than hoped for, not in small part due to increased regulation and scrutiny over safety issues.

Its shares fell 9.1% to 28.90 Hong Kong dollars, equivalent to US$3.68, in early trade on Thursday .

"Although Pony AI appears on track to achieve its full-year 2026 robotaxi fleet target of 3,500 units, we see increasing downside risk to its domestic fleet expansion from 2027 onward due to a tightening of China's autonomous vehicle licensing regime," said Deutsche Bank analyst Bin Wang in a note.

After a March 2026 incident in Wuhan, where more than 100 Baidu's Apollo Go robotaxis were stalled by a system outage, China temporarily suspended new robotaxi permit approvals pending a nationwide safety review.

Approvals gradually resumed in July but the process has become more stringent, requiring municipalities to complete corrective measures and obtain sign-offs, Wang added. That is likely to delay deployments and slow fleet expansion across China's robotaxi industry, DB added.

The company's management, though, believes the regulatory environment is turning positive and recent policies are aimed at creating a standardized national framework with a uniform, high safety bar, Citi analysts wrote in a note.

This favors operators with proven technology and safety records in tier-1 cities such as Pony AI, they added.

Citi maintained its buy and high risk rating for the stock with an unchanged target price of $22.7. Deutsche Bank also maintained its buy rating but trimmed its target price to $7.00 from $14.10.

Write to Jiahui Huang at jiahui.huang@wsj.com

data.title: Nasdaq, Dow, S&P 500 Futures Climb Ahead Of Anthropic’s Record Debut: SLS, GLD, TTWO, UNH In Focus
data.description:
Key points:
  • The AI company also upsized its offering, selling approximately 980 million shares, bringing the amount raised to $81.3 billion. 
  • The Federal Reserve’s minutes released on Wednesday weighed on market sentiment as policymakers flagged inflation concerns and AI risks.
  • Comments from policymakers weighed on precious metals, sending gold and silver prices to their lowest levels in more than a year.

U.S. stock futures traded higher overnight late Wednesday as markets geared up for Anthropic’s public trading.

As of 10:49 p.m. EST, Dow futures climbed 0.41%, while the S&P 500 futures gained 0.63% and Nasdaq-100 futures climbed more than 1%.

On Wednesday, the three U.S. benchmark indexes closed mixed. The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed more than 650 points to end the session 1.11% lower, while the S&P 500 fell 0.23%. The Nasdaq Composite closed in the green, ending the session 0.42% higher.

IndexMoveClose
Dow Jones Industrial Average-1.11%50,198.17
S&P 500-0.23%7,323.63
Nasdaq Composite0.42%24,429.88

Key US Market Drivers

This week, all eyes have been on Anthropic’s debut on stock markets, which begins trading on Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker “ANT.”

The AI company priced its initial public offering at $83 a share, above the expected range, as per a post from the company. It also upsized its offering, selling approximately 980 million shares, bringing the amount raised to $81.3 billion and surpassing SpaceX’s (SPCX) record IPO.

Ross Gerber, Co-Founder, CEO and CIO at Gerber Kawasaki, congratulated the company on its upcoming debut, saying in a post on X, “Incredible. Congrats Anthropic. Let the AI era truly begin. $ANT.”

Pro Capital (BRR) CEO Anthony Pompliano said in a post on X, “The Anthropic IPO is going to remind everyone how insane markets can be sometimes.”

The AI trade has been struggling in recent weeks amid a technology rout and a fallout in Nvidia Corp.’s (NVDA) dominance following CEO Jensen Huang’s infidelity reports and subsequent resignation.

“It’ll be an important barometer for investors’ AI appetite,” Callie Cox, director of investment strategy at Plancorp, said to CNBC about the IPO.

“AI stocks desperately need some wind at their backs, too ... Wall Street needs a sign that investors still believe in the potential for AI beyond already-elevated expectations,” Cox added.

Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve’s minutes released on Wednesday weighed on market sentiment as policymakers flagged inflation concerns and AI risks.

The central bank’s policymakers called artificial intelligence “a material source of inflation risk” in their latest minutes from the October meeting, adding that “off-balance-sheet leasing commitments and circular financing arrangements among AI-related firms could amplify losses if returns on AI investment were to disappoint.”

Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said in an interview with CNBC on Wednesday that the central bank needs to “shock people” with at least a half-percentage-point interest rate hike in the December meeting as inflationary concerns continue to mount.

A day earlier, St. Louis Fed president Alberto Musalem said that the Federal Reserve may need several rate hikes to control inflation ​and should act soon.

Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco President Mary Daly also noted that further interest rate hikes will be needed to ensure inflation returns to the central bank's 2% target. However, Daly suggested adopting a more “measured pace” to evaluate shifting economic conditions.

The comments sparked a selloff in markets and weighed on precious metals, sending gold and silver prices to their lowest levels in more than a year.

As per Bitcoin Archive, gold and silver’s 10% drop over the last nine days have wiped out $3.3 trillion in market value, larger than Nvidia’s over $1 trillion loss since Huang’s exit.

Meanwhile, markets will be watching out for weekly jobless claims on Thursday, and earnings from Walmart Inc. (WMT) and clothing retailer Gap Inc. (GAP).

Trending Tickers To Watch 

SELLAS Life Sciences Group Inc. (SLS): The company’s shares plunged nearly 13% in the overnight session, paring phenomenal gains from Tuesday when the company revealed positive topline results for Phase 3 Regal trial of its cancer vaccine galinpepimut-S (GPS) in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) after it announced a discounted public offering worth $150 million.

SPDR Gold Shares ETF (GLD): The gold-linked exchange-traded fund was on the retail radar amid a steep decline in the price of the yellow metal amid a rising dollar and Fed’s hawkish comments.

Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. (TTWO): The gaming company’s shares surged at close and continued to climb overnight after its Grand Theft Auto VI game garnered overwhelmingly positive early reviews and its Metacritic score came in at 99 out of 100.

UnitedHealth Group Inc. (UNH): Shares of the company fell over 10% after Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) proposed tighter Medicare and Medicaid anti-fraud audits and oversight, potentially increasing compliance and documentation requirements for managed care providers such as UnitedHealth.

Other Market Trends 

Among ETFs tracking benchmark indexes, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) edged higher in the overnight session.

The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield was trading at 5.056%, while the 30-year yield was at 5.398%.

The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) was up 0.19% amid ‘bullish’ sentiment.

Asian markets opened mixed on Thursday, with South Korea's KOSPI and China’s SSE Composite trading lower at the time of writing, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 was in the green. Australian stocks also traded lower at the open.

data.title: Chicago soybeans ease for fourth straight session, wheat, corn fall
data.description:
Chicago soybeans fell for a fourth straight session on Thursday, weighed down by weaker crude oil prices, which made soybean oil a less attractive biodiesel feedstock.

The most-traded soybean contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) fell 0.29% to $12.13-1/4 a bushel at 0347 GMT.

Chicago wheat declined 0.34% to $5.84 a bushel. The contract lost 3.97% in the previous session, its biggest daily drop since September 2023.

CBOT corn fell for three straight sessions and lost 0.57% to its lowest since June 30, at $4.33 a bushel.

Brent crude oil prices fell 0.24%, making biofuels made from soybeans and corn less attractive.

US cash millfeed values were mostly steady on Wednesday, as demand in some markets helped keep a floor under prices, according to dealers

Ahead of Thursday's weekly export sales report from the US Department of Agriculture, analysts expected the government to report net export sales of US corn in the week to November 12 at 1.2 million to 2 million metric tons, wheat exports at 200,000 to 400,000 tons and soybean exports at 1 million to 2 million tons.

Recent rainfall in northeastern Brazil has kept forecasts for the country's 2026/27 soybean crop at record levels, even in a year marked by a strong El Niño, AgRural's founder said.

Farm office FranceAgriMer on Wednesday sharply raised its monthly forecast for French soft wheat exports outside the European Union this season, after demand for French supplies surged as Russia's war in Ukraine disrupted Black Sea trade.

China's corn imports in October stood at 490,000 tons, 36.8% higher than in the same period a year ago, government data showed.
